assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson closed the Standard Model's central open question and was an empirical discovery of the kind that sits at the centre of a prize: a new particle, observed independently by two detectors. The theoretical prediction was recognised in 2013, but the experimental discovery has not been, and it is both original as a feat of measurement and lasting in impact through the ongoing coupling and mass programme.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the hard part: a collaboration of thousands. The supplied names are the founding and leading figures of the two experiments (Jenni for ATLAS, Virdee for CMS) plus Gianotti as ATLAS spokesperson at the time of the announcement. Della Negra, the other CMS founder, is a strong alternative and I do not claim this choice is uniquely correct; the configuration fairly covers both experiments but is open to dispute.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: two independent experiments, confirmation of spin-parity and couplings with the full Run 1 to Run 3 data, and a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely, more than a decade after discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would accept an experiment-leader trio as a fair representation of a very large collaboration.
Which of Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee and Gianotti made the most decisive contributions is not settled by the supplied text and I rely on general knowledge of their roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised to unprecedented stability and accuracy by Ye's group, have redefined the frontier of precision measurement, reaching fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enabling relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The idea is original, the realisation clear, and the impact on metrology and fundamental physics is lasting.
assessment.attribution: A clean two-person configuration. Katori invented the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye led the strontium clock to record performance. Others (for example Ludlow, Hinkley and Lemke at NIST/JILA, Takamoto) contributed, but the conceptual and leading-experimental credit supports two laureates well. Ye's earlier frequency-comb link to the 2005 prize is a possible but minor framing issue.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent laboratories confirm the performance, and the redefinition of the second is being prepared with optical clocks.
uncertainties: Whether the 2005 recognition of frequency-comb work makes the committee regard clocks as already honoured.
Share of credit relative to the ion-clock and Sr-clock competitors is based on my own knowledge, not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator opened a whole class of topological matter: a prediction from simple band theory followed by a clean experimental realisation. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and the quantum Hall effect, but not this materials realisation. Originality and impact are high, spanning spintronics, topological superconductors and Majorana searches.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step in 2005; Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, following Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's proposal, whose absence from the credited names is a significant attribution weakness. Three-person structure of two theorists and one experimentalist is natural, but a fair account must recognise the omitted contributions.
assessment.maturity: Mature: confirmed in several material systems and by independent groups, with the interpretation stable for nearly two decades.
uncertainties: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not among the credited names and their role in the HgTe proposal is disputed in priority terms.
Whether the committee views this as an extension of the 2016 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, later tied to the blazar TXS 0506+056 and to NGC 1068, opened neutrino astronomy at TeV to PeV energies. This is a clear, discovery-driven result using an instrument of novel scale, and the impact on multi-messenger astrophysics is growing.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is widely seen as the intellectual driver of the project; Karle and Spiering are well-established early leaders. IceCube is a large collaboration, so any trio would be a simplification, and the roles of others (for example Gaisser, Waxman and Bahcall's theoretical predictions) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: the diffuse flux is confirmed to high significance, with source identification still developing and the interpretation of sources not settled.
uncertainties: The source of most of the flux remains unidentified.
Whether the committee would prefer to wait for a firmer source association.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer and MacDonald prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle bilayer graphene, created the field of moiré quantum matter. The prediction-then-discovery arc is exactly the sort of clean theory and experiment pairing that gives a prize clarity, and the impact on condensed-matter research is large.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. Cao and the other first authors are not credited and a Nobel can honour only three, so a configuration of experimenter plus two theorists is defensible. Others (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, Dean, Kim, Young) are not in the supplied names and credit may be contested.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: reproduced by many groups, but interpretation of superconductivity and correlated phases is still developing, and the discovery is under a decade old, so recognition could be premature.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains debated.
Priority between the continuum-model theory groups and the omission of other pioneers is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are direct empirical evidence of the shadow of a black hole, an observation of fundamental importance to gravitation. As a theorist working on black holes I find the result notable, though the 2020 prize already recognised black-hole physics, and the images confirm rather than overturn the general-relativity expectation.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT, Falcke proposed using the shadow and was a key scientific leader, and Zensus built the European VLBI infrastructure. The EHT collaboration is large and the individual contributions (for example Bower, Johnson, Narayan, Broderick) are not well separated in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense of two sources, multiple epochs, and polarisation, but still new, with the physics of the images (spin, accretion model) not fully pinned down.
uncertainties: Interpretation of the ring and its constraints on the black-hole metric is model-dependent.
The 2020 prize may shape the committee's appetite for a second black-hole prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the spectrum of primordial fluctuations, and the quantum origin of structure is a remarkable idea, with the CMB acoustic pattern supporting the scalar spectrum. As a cosmologist and string theorist I recognise its centrality but also its limits: the specific inflaton remains unknown and there is no detection of primordial gravitational waves.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is difficult: Starobinsky, Sato, Albrecht and Steinhardt, Hawking, Bardeen and Guth-Pi are all connected, and Starobinsky is not among the credited names. Guth, Linde and Mukhanov are a plausible group but not an uncontested one, which weakens the case as a prize configuration.
assessment.maturity: The paradigm is supported but not decisively tested; competing alternatives are not fully excluded, and a key prediction (tensor modes) has not been seen. This could be premature.
uncertainties: Absence of Starobinsky and other originators in the credited names.
No direct evidence of the inflationary tensor spectrum.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a conceptually original application of quantum foundations with real-world technology and demonstrations including satellite links. Its theoretical foundations (BB84 and the E91 entanglement-based protocol) are clear and lasting, and the 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests makes the follow-on natural.
assessment.attribution: BB84 by Bennett and Brassard is clearly decisive; Ekert independently proposed the entanglement-based scheme in 1991. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not among the credited names and is a known priority question. The three-name structure is otherwise fair.
assessment.maturity: The principle is established and many experiments exist, though practical security under device imperfections and the commercial deployment are still evolving, so the prize case rests on principle more than on technology.
uncertainties: Wiesner's conjugate coding as precursor is not credited.
Whether the committee judges QKD to be physics discovery or a primarily information-science invention.
